source_grounding.call_chain_traced: GET /cluster/telemetry -> actix get_cluster_telemetry (src/actix/api/cluster_api.rs:204) -> details_level = params.details_level.unwrap_or_default().max(2) [0/1 silently clamped, never rejected; no 0..10 validation exists] -> all_peers = channel_service.id_to_address keys -> in the sandbox's standalone deployment id_to_address is EMPTY (src/main.rs:299-317 populates it only when is_distributed_deployment; channel_service.rs:47 defaults to empty map) -> zero peer futures -> telemetries = [] -> DistributedTelemetryData::resolve_telemetries -> newest_telemetry(&[]) = None -> StorageError::service_error('Could not get telemetry from cluster') (distributed_telemetry.rs:157-158) -> HTTP 500 with the observed body. The 500 is therefore parameter-independent: identical for details_level 0/1/10/11, for every timeout value, and for parameter-less calls — all confirmed in the session logs.
source_grounding.outcome_note: validation_absent holds for the details_level domain specifically: the REST face performs no range validation of the documented(-in-contract) 0..10 domain — ClusterTelemetryParams (cluster_api.rs:42-46) puts #[validate(range(min = 1))] on timeout but nothing on details_level; values <2 are silently clamped by .max(2) (cluster_api.rs:217-220) under an explicit TODO ('For now, we only handle details_level >= 2 / TODO(cluster telemetry): Handle lower levels', lines 23-25), and values above the recorded maximum (11) pass through unchallenged. The internal gRPC face (qdrant_internal_api.rs:90-94) shows the contrasting disposition: explicit invalid_argument rejection for <2, backed by the comment at telemetry.rs:230 ('This only happens when details_level is < 2, which we explicitly fail'). Separately, the observed 500 itself is NOT a validation question and NOT parameter-dependent: its proximate cause is the standalone deployment shape (empty id_to_address by construction in single-node mode), which the source documents descriptively (main.rs:284-286 'In single-node mode a default-configured service is returned') but nowhere declares as an intended 500 for this endpoint — no comment in the handler marks the standalone 500 as intentional, so by_design_in_source is not satisfied for the 500. Whether the parameter-independence of the 500 (deployment-shape dependency) demotes the Type3 attribution is left to the chain-auditor; the raw observation and its mechanism are both fully established.
